findings.what: Three rules that the requirement states as a closed set, a whole value or exactly one are still held against one neighbour only, as in the two earlier extra passes. (a) 'A chain of at least 3 characters only of *, x, X': every Ch sweep writes the text as <place> + chain + <slot> + '9' + <end>. The digit 9 after the slot makes a text with a widened chain a literal anyway, so a widening of the set by any character other than a digit cannot be seen. Mutants that stay GREEN (fast subset 6 of 6, and the whole bytes file plus six guard files 151 of 151): x54 (the chain may also hold - or .), y22 (also the letter y), y23 (also +), y24 (also =), y25 (also #); y21 (_) is red and x53 (digits) is red, so only the characters that happen to stand in a row are held. Real code and mutant differ on token=xxy, token=xyxy, token=x+x, token=x=x, token=##x, token=x-x, token=---, token=xxx- (all refused by the real code, stored by the mutants). (b) 'The whole value is one of 26 words': a word is tried with a digit after it (word9) and in rows with a prefix of letters (wrong-password), never with a . or - on either side. Mutants y19 (a word followed by . - or _ is still a word) and y20 (the same in front) stay GREEN, 151 of 151. Differ on password=password. , token=test- , token=-secret , token=.test (refused by the real code, stored by the mutants). (c) Form F1, 'exactly one space' between BEGIN and CERTIFICATE in the one stored header: C10 holds the case, the truncated header, the dashes (six on either side) and the label, but no row with two spaces or a tab. Mutants z01b (one to three spaces) and z02 (a tab in place of the space) stay GREEN, 151 of 151. Differ on the header with two spaces and on the header with a tab (refused by the real code, stored by the mutants).
